positive.prompt: Audit the GitHub settings on my repo and tell me which best practices I'm missing
Set up branch protection and security features on my new open-source repo
What is actually enabled on this repository? Are rulesets and Dependabot configured?
I'm preparing my .NET library repo for its first NuGet release, so harden the GitHub config first

negative.prompt: Set up a CI pipeline that builds the project and runs our tests on every push
Commit this work and open a pull request
Check this login handler for SQL injection and weak session handling

evals.prompt: Review the GitHub setup of this repo from the captured audit in audit-snapshot.jsonl (you have no network access), and write the findings and an ordered action plan to REPORT.md.
evals.expected_output: A REPORT.md with evidence-backed findings, an ordered plan that respects dependency order, approval tiers for risky steps, and no re-proposal of declined or deferred decisions
expectations: REPORT.md flags the unprotected default branch (no rulesets, legacy branch protection absent) as a high-severity finding and cites the audit evidence for it
REPORT.md flags Dependabot alerts and security updates being disabled, code scanning not configured, and private vulnerability reporting disabled
The plan puts CI (or a workflow that reports a status check) before activating a ruleset that requires that check, or explicitly defers the required-check rule until CI exists
The plan enables immutable releases before the first release and marks ruleset activation and immutable releases as needing explicit per-item approval
REPORT.md does not propose required signed commits, and does not set up an AI reviewer or the CI/release pipeline now; deferred items are listed as deferred with what blocks them
REPORT.md lists items the snapshot cannot show (two-factor authentication, nuget.org account state) as unknown or as needing the maintainer, instead of marking them OK
No settings were changed: the run issued no mutating gh command and made no direct edits other than creating REPORT.md
